paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the LORD is the only God, and He is the One who made you. Isaiah 44 opens right after a warning of destruction, and the LORD still says, "Do not be afraid, O Jacob My servant" (Isa 44:2). He calls Himself "the first and the last," and says, "there is no God but Me" (Isa 44:6). So the God who stands over everything is the same God who formed His people from the womb.

Now look at the idol maker. He burns half the wood to warm up and cook, then carves the other half and says, "Save me, for you are my god" (Isa 44:16-17). I can't even get a cookie to hold still for me, so asking a block of wood to rescue me? Idols are things we make, and a thing we make can't carry us. Whatever you're tempted to lean on besides the LORD, ask what Isaiah's idol maker never asked: "Shall I bow down to a block of wood?" (Isa 44:19).

The best part comes at the end. The LORD says, "I will never forget you," and that He has blotted out transgressions "like a cloud" (Isa 44:21-22). Then He says, "Return to Me, for I have redeemed you." I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and I can tell you that being remembered beats everything. You don't come back to the LORD to earn it. You come back because He already did the rescuing, and that's why even the mountains break into song (Isa 44:23).
